public_rationale: The evidence establishes both cost concerns and real reliability problems. It does not establish their relative causal effects. limitations: The deployment survey was commissioned by an AI vendor and measures reported experiences.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The massive expense of running generative models hasn't been what limits their deployment or success; the limit is that they are neither artificial intelligence nor capable of the meaningful outcomes that would make them the next smartphone.

statement.excerpt: In any case, the massive expense of running generative models hasn’t been the limiter on their deployment or success — you can blame that on the fact that they, as a piece of technology, are neither artificial intelligence nor capable of providing the kind of meaningful outcomes that would make them the next Smartphone.

our_interpretation: The testable causal reading is that operating expense was not a material binding constraint on deployment or success, while capability and reliability limitations were.
The statement is retrospective through January 29, 2025. It supplies no starting date, so none is imposed.
I do not turn the philosophical label artificial intelligence or the smartphone comparison into an invented performance threshold.
This concerns technology-wide deployment constraints, not a stated financial metric for a particular company.
criteria.support_condition: Comparative deployment evidence shows that lowering operating costs did little to remove deployment constraints, while capability or reliability improvements materially removed them.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible deployment evidence isolates model operating expense as a material binding constraint, or otherwise establishes that the proposed capability-based explanation is materially wrong.
